spec_readings.quote: ClaimNextEligible from W claimers (W = 1x, then 2x worker_counts)
spec_readings.reading: W = worker_counts x worker_multiple; each worker is one claim loop with its own owner id holding one claim at a time, the production shape of one claim loop per collector Deployment.

spec_readings.quote: at least one synthetic scope is held at its budget ... grants per budget bucket never exceed quota_budget
spec_readings.reading: The quota kind gets an at-budget scope with budget+extra items and a below-budget scope with budget-1 items. no_overshoot passes when no (kind, scope, hour) bucket is above budget and at least one bucket reached it. Items still held above budget at the end are reported as quota_held_items and excluded from drain_to_zero; a new hour bucket may drain them legitimately.

spec_readings.quote: some are pinned and then outlive the commit deadline; some are pinned after reclaim (stale)
spec_readings.reading: A seeded share pins before completing; a short pin whose deadline passes while the lease lives must still complete; half of the abandoned claims are pinned past their lease and the reaper must wait for the pin; stale pins rotate into the step-9 writes and must be fence-rejected.

spec_readings.quote: a seeded share of terminal calls is replayed once after an injected timeout
spec_readings.reading: Terminal means CompleteClaim and FailClaimTerminal. The first call gets a 1 ms deadline, then one replay on a fresh deadline must ack. Release and FailClaimRetryable are not replayed: after another worker re-claims the item, rejection is correct and belongs to step 9.

spec_readings.quote: a seeded share of workers keeps writing with an old fencing token after their claim was reaped and re-claimed
spec_readings.reading: An abandoned claim's worker writes once (heartbeat, complete, fail_terminal, or pin) after the client has seen the item re-granted at a higher token. Success aborts; any code other than the fence rejection fails the criterion.

spec_readings.quote: every expired lease is reclaimed within lease_ttl + reap_interval + one reap pass
spec_readings.reading: Measured per abandoned claim as finished_at of the expired claim row minus the later of lease_expires_at and the commit pin, against reap_interval + the longest measured reap pass + 1 s + clock skew (lease_ttl is already inside lease_expires_at). The 5 s requeue delay applies after the reap and is not in the bound.

spec_readings.quote: no eligible item waits longer than starvation_bound_seconds; no scope goes unclaimed while below budget
spec_readings.reading: The longest ClaimNextEligible call (issued or idle) must stay under the bound, and every backlog scope must get a grant inside the window. Enqueue-to-first-claim wait over a 100,000-item backlog is minutes by construction and is not judged.

spec_readings.quote: stop issuing work, let reap and replay finish, confirm zero nonterminal synthetic items and zero live synthetic claims
spec_readings.reading: After the window the chaos mix stops; workers keep claiming and completing the remaining backlog until every non-quota-held item is terminal, no claim is live, and every armed stale writer has fired.

spec_readings.quote: peak nonterminal workflow_work_items depth from production history
spec_readings.reading: Production tables carry planner statistics, a freshly seeded one does not. After seeding the harness waits read-only (bounded, default 5m) for autovacuum to analyze workflow_work_items; stats_ready=false records a window run on cold statistics.

spec_readings.quote: collector instance: synth-8875-rehearsal-leg-1 on an enumerated synthetic instance with an existing claim-capable kind ... The lane proves this first with a dry claim that must return idle while real work exists.
spec_readings.reading: The harness claims only on synth-8875-rehearsal-leg-1, which keeps the synthetic prefix but sits outside the census instance family (synth-8875-rehearsal-instance-%), so the baseline ignores the satellite's declaration row for it and no harness item names it before the seed. The dry claim on it returns idle by construction: on live it shows only that no item names this instance yet, not that the selector excludes real work. The report marks the probe VACUOUS on both targets; the arbiter rules on the instance at the live-run review.

spec_readings.quote: created count = terminal count + live count at every sample
spec_readings.reading: Each sample counts synthetic item rows, which are terminal plus non-terminal by construction, and requires rows >= created. Rows may briefly exceed created because an admitted advisory round commits before its count is added. After the run, every client-acked terminal item must be terminal in the database.

spec_readings.quote: satellite database CPU, connection count, and replication-lag limits
spec_readings.reading: The live ceiling on lock waiters counts core's database only (ESHU_CONTENTION_PG_LOCK_DATABASE=eshu). A local in-tree advisory round queues up to 24 sessions on pg_advisory_xact_lock by design, so the local ceiling sits above the advisory goroutines plus W.

isolation_probe.detail: dry claim idle on synth-8875-rehearsal-leg-1, which is not an enumerated live instance (synth-8875-tfstate, synth-8875-pkgreg) and names no harness item before the seed; the satellite declares it from its own instances file. It shows no work is claimable on this instance yet, not that real work is excluded.
